Phase 4/7 CheckpointStore spec must treat retention/archival and schema-versioning/migration as first-class parts of the contract, not implementation details deferred to whichever backend is chosen - LangGraph's own open issues (#536 schema migration, #1138 unbounded growth) are direct evidence this is unsolved even in a mature, genuinely local-capable checkpointer

Mastra's Workspace is the strongest match found to LabLaunchPad's planned adapters/tools boundary combined with a policy layer - worth citing directly when Phase 8 (Capability Registry) and the tool-boundary Policy Gate design are formalized

First draft of the LangGraph local-first verdict (HYBRID, citing a Postgres/Redis production requirement) overstated the SDK's own dependency; corrected to LOCAL_CAPABLE after re-reading the Checkpointer interface directly, per user feedback. Applies the same evidence-discipline rule used for the Youtu-Agent correction: re-check a finding against primary sources before treating it as settled, regardless of source (a user's steer is not exempt from this either - the correction itself was verified against LangGraph's own docs, not accepted on assertion alone)

First draft recorded a simple core/ee two-way license split for Mastra; deeper research found a third, distinguishable platform tier (Studio/observability/Memory Gateway, commercially metered).
